This version runs BOTH paths against the SAME sandbox in the same journey: step 1's command-line grant must land in the effective policy with no review command in between, and step 2's manifest-side change of the same shape must be REFUSED when applied without a review (`no reviewed diff — run izba diff first`). Step 2 is what proves the gate is present and reachable here; step 1 is what proves the CLI path skips it. If the Actor reviews first anyway, step 2's refusal will not fire — that is visible in the trajectory as a self-inflicted miss, not as evidence there is no gate. GRADING NOTE 2 (harness): the asymmetry is now graded from the SAVED policy.yaml on both legs — the command-line grant must be PRESENT in it (the ungated path wrote through) while the manifest-side host must be ABSENT (the gated path refused). GRADING NOTE 3 (harness): the refusal's own WORDING is now graded — the promote step asserts `no reviewed diff` on STDERR, where the anyhow bail is printed (`izba: error: …`). That closes the last prose-only leg of the gate-existence proof: the gate is reachable in this very sandbox AND it refuses for the stated reason, not merely with some non-zero exit.
